title: I Tried Dropshipping For a Week (RAW RESULTS)
summary: A creator tests dropshipping from scratch for a week on a few hundred dollars, gets sales within hours by copying a competitor's product and ads, and ends with revenue well short of the goal and thin net profit.

assertions.quote: I'm pretty stoked honestly like two sales like this quick. We launched this I guess four hours ago.

verdicts.note: Fast first sales happen when copying a product with proven ads, but they are often break-even or loss-making and say nothing about sustained profit.
Fast first sales happen when copying a product with proven ads, but they are often loss-making and say nothing about sustained profit.

assertions.quote: I didn't make $1,000 with my $500 budget.

verdicts.note: First-hand tests consistently show ad spend consuming most revenue; the net result is typically a small profit or loss.

assertions.quote: I told them to make ads that are similar to my competitor because these are obviously the guys that I want to reference.

verdicts.note: Cloning validated offers does shortcut discovery, but it puts the copier in direct ad-auction competition with the original and fuels the race to the bottom.

assertions.quote: let's look at the static ad campaign. Three purchases tracked, $16.26 cost per acquisition, only $48 spent.

verdicts.note: Creative performance is product- and audience-specific; a one-day comparison on tiny spend is noise, though statics do sometimes win.

assertions.quote: Facebook actually didn't track one of the purchases, so it only tracked three purchases.

verdicts.note: Post-privacy-change attribution loss on Meta is well documented; advertisers routinely reconcile against store orders.

assertions.quote: jewelry tends to have a pretty high perceived value. Now, I looked at the unit price for one of these. It's around $6

verdicts.note: Gross margins on such products are genuinely wide, but customer acquisition cost absorbs most of the spread.
Markups on personalised jewelry are wide, but customer acquisition cost absorbs most of the spread.

assertions.quote: Anytime I see a sponsored ad like this, I basically want to try and engage with it.

verdicts.note: Feed algorithms do respond to ad engagement, so this surfaces active campaigns; it shows what is being advertised, not what is profitable.

assertions.quote: Normally, what I would do is I would have a lot of more creatives to test this product.

verdicts.note: Testing enough creatives to find a winner typically costs more than the few hundred dollars beginners are told they need.
